payload.summary: The current branch already compiles and already has the denitrification-test confounder removed, so I reject the two compile-break amendments and the nitrate-test amendment as no longer matching the code under review. I also reject the unused `HighDensity` variant amendment because it is dead-code cleanup without a demonstrated behavioral defect. I accept the Ca/Mg defensive-guard amendment and the snapshot reproduction-suppression drift amendment because both are still real robustness/diagnostic issues.

votes.rationale: The current codebase has single definitions of `density_repro_factor`, `tan_repro_factor`, and `no2_repro_factor`, and `snapshot.rs` already defines `dominant_repro_suppression`. `cargo test -p tank_core snapshot` builds and passes, so this compile-break claim does not match the branch as it exists now.

The described confounder has already been removed: the active and control cases now both use zero nutrient stores in `long_horizon_denitrification_state`, and the targeted integration test passes. This amendment is technically reasonable in principle, but there is no remaining defect to fix in the current branch.

GH already uses a defensive floor, but Ca/Mg still divide by the raw minima. Even if validation normally rejects zero Ca/Mg minima, `molt_mineral_modifier` can still produce non-finite output on zero thresholds, so extending the same guard is a sound robustness fix.

This points out unused dead code, but it does not identify a concrete correctness, safety, or robustness failure. Without a specific event path that is semantically wrong today, removing or forcing use of `EventCause::HighDensity` would be cleanup churn rather than a necessary amendment.

This is another compile-break report that does not match the current branch. There is no duplicate import/redefinition in `snapshot.rs`, the helper functions are not duplicated, and the snapshot test target builds successfully.

`repro_dominant_suppression` currently re-implements the reproduction model in `snapshot.rs` instead of reusing the real readiness logic. It omits the molt-stress factor, collapses TAN and nitrite into a single bucket, and uses its own thresholding, so it can disagree with the actual readiness calculation and mislead debugging or telemetry.
